rationales.a: Atrial systole produces the preceding a wave, not x descent.
rationales.c: Ventricular diastole and tricuspid opening are associated with y descent.
rationales.d: Joint diastole is not the phase represented by the x descent.

marrow__PHYSIO_CH28_Q025.takeaway: The Bainbridge reflex raises heart rate when increased venous return distends the right atrium.
marrow__PHYSIO_CH28_Q025.displayText:
The Bainbridge reflex raises heart rate when increased venous return distends the right atrium.

Reflex responsible for tachycardia during right atrial distension is Bainbridge reflex.

Atrial Reflex Control of Heart Rate: The Bainbridge Reflex

+ The stretch receptors of the atria that elicit the Bainbridge reflex transmit their afferent signals
through the vagus nerves to the medulla of the brain.

+ Then efferent signals are transmitted back through vagal and sympathetic nerves to increase
heart rate and strength of heart contraction.

Bezold-Jarisch Reflex:

emphasis: The Bainbridge reflex raises heart rate when increased venous return distends the right atrium

rationales.a: The J-receptor reflex is associated with pulmonary interstitial events and may cause bradycardia.
rationales.b: Cushing reflex responds to raised intracranial pressure.
rationales.c: Bezold–Jarisch reflex is triggered by ventricular afferents and classically causes bradycardia/hypotension.

+ The p wave in the ECG represents atrial depolarization, which causes contraction of the atria,
represented by the ‘a’ wave in the JVP. Atrial contraction causes final filling of the ventricles
(fourth phase of ventricular diastole)

517 

+ Atrial contraction is followed by the closure of the mitral valve, which causes the first-heart
sound.

+ This is followed by the isovolumetric contraction of the ventricle, which causes ¢ wave in JVP,
due to bulging of the tricuspid valve. This is followed by the rapid ejection phase of the ventricle.

+ The T wave of ECG occurs during ventricular repolarization, which is followed by the opening of
the mitral valve, followed by rapid filling phase of the ventricle (second phase of ventricular

diastole).

Note: Passive rapid filling occurs as the mitral valve opens just before atrial contraction occurs.
emphasis: After the P wave, atrial contraction precedes AV conduction delay, ventricular depolarization and ventricular systole; the printed sequence is 1–2–4–3

rationales.a: This places rapid ventricular filling before the T wave, although ventricular repolarization precedes mitral opening and rapid filling.
rationales.c: Starting with rapid filling puts a late-diastolic event before the atrial contraction that follows the P wave.
rationales.d: This puts ventricular filling before S1/AV-valve closure; filling follows ejection and mitral opening.
